planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; this vigorous miniature tolerates a bit more sun than most hostas without losing leaf color.

directions: A Mark Zilis hybrid (a gold sport of 'Blue Dimples' crossed with 'Shining Tot') selected by Bob Solberg, Appletini is the miniature cultivar from which the sport 'Tiki Bar' later arose. It forms a tight mound of thick, smooth, waxy leaves that emerge yellow in spring and mature to apple-green by summer, reaching only about 6 inches tall and 14 inches wide. Purple flowers appear on short scapes in late summer, and the heavy leaf substance gives good resistance to slug damage. Its small scale suits edging, troughs, and containers in a shaded garden.

common_name: Imperial Banner Toad Lily (White-Centered Variegated Toad Lily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; warm root temperatures help the variegation express fully.

directions: Introduced by Terra Nova Nurseries, Imperial Banner arose as a mutation of Tricyrtis 'Empress' and is the parent from which the compact sport 'White Waves' was later selected. Glossy green leaves carry a bold central patch of creamy-white variegation edged in deep green, held on dark stems in an attractive two-foot clump. Short terminal spikes of light lavender flowers heavily spotted in dark purple top the foliage from midsummer into early fall. Because the variegation is unstable, prune out any all-green reverted shoots promptly to keep the patterned foliage dominant.

common_name: Ruby Earrings Hosta (Yellow Ear-Shaped Hosta with Ruby-Red Petioles)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with some morning sun to keep the yellow coloring and red petiole contrast strong.

directions: Introduced in 2021 by Bob Solberg of Green Hill Farm, Ruby Earrings is the sibling selection from which the upright yellow sport 'Cherry Cheesecake' was later bred. It forms an upright clump of deeply cupped, lightly puckered, medium-yellow leaves with exaggerated ear-like lobes at the base, the ruby-red petiole color piercing roughly halfway into each leaf for a jewel-toned effect. Mature clumps reach about 10 inches tall and 22 inches across. Grow with some morning sun for the strongest yellow color and red contrast, and divide as the clump becomes congested.

common_name: Twice as Nice Hosta (Yellow-Centered, Blue-Margined Fragrant Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; some morning sun helps hold the bright yellow leaf center.

directions: A tetraploid sport of 'Ambrosia' bred by Bob Solberg of Green Hill Farm, Twice as Nice is the parent from which the brighter, glossier sport 'Even Better' later arose. It forms a compact mound of blue-green leaves with heavy substance and a bright yellow medial center, the wide blue-green margins giving strong two-tone contrast. Fragrant, pale lavender flowers rise on scapes up to 41 inches tall from mid-July into August, later than most hosta bloom. Mature clumps reach about 20 inches tall and 45 inches wide; divide every few years as clumps become congested.
